questions.q: How did IBM put customers first, according to the summary?
a: Entry-level staff resolved complaints within a day
It offered the lowest prices in the industry
It replaced salespeople with self-service tools
It published a toll-free customer hotline first
questions.why: Lesson 1 says IBM staff handled customer complaints within 24 hours, building trust.

questions.q: What is the lip service trap described in the summary?
a: Claiming to care about staff without actually training them
Rewarding one worker with a monthly title
Promising customers service you cannot deliver
Hiring consultants instead of listening to staff
questions.why: Lesson 2 names lip service and gimmicks as false ways of caring for employees.

questions.q: How do excellent companies treat their employees?
a: They invest in development and expect a lot from them
They monitor schedules and enforce strict rules
They keep teams small to avoid extra benefits
They reward individuals with symbolic prizes
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends a people-centered workplace with training and informal communication.

questions.q: What do the best companies emphasize beyond financial numbers?
a: Clear values such as service and innovation
Aggressive growth targets and market share
Quarterly reports for shareholders
Cost controls across every department
questions.why: Lesson 3 says firms focused on broader values like quality and service outperform number-driven ones.
